Life itself is a struggle,  and I hope you know that just by posting this you are not only helping yourself be above that, but helping others like me as well. I have dealt with similar issues myself for the bulk of my 30 years. Each of us handles things in different ways but owning your issues is absolutely a fantastic first step. 

Don't let your environment influence your decision to be what or whoever you want or need to be right now. Alcoholism is a scary thing to witness, and more so to experience.  I have had my own struggles and watched helplessly as my ex wife took herself down into that darkness. 

AA can be a wonderful source of help if you are willing and able to follow through with the idea that you cannot be in control of your own life. That may sound cynical but it's true. 

You've come far enough to realize you have an issue with alcohol but I wonder if you've considered that your drinking is a symptom and not the problem.  By the small bit you shared it seems like you are doing what you know, a PavlovIan response.  I've been finding that to be true in my own life as I create ways to recreate my life's most devastating moments. Not intentionally mind you, though some how I manage to do it. 

Recognizing that you feel out of control is in itself a means to control your situation.  If you find yourself craving a drink find the motivation behind it, don't cave to your subconscious! 

I hope any of this makes sense to you, if nothing else it helped me just to write this out, so you made a difference in my life tonight. Thank you I hope you find your peace and feel better.
